description: Golden Set v4 - Manually verified answers from actual documents

tests.question: When do I become vested in company contributions?
tests.source_reference: SPD page 18, 'When You Vest in Company Contributions'
key_facts: Your own contributions are immediately 100% vested
Company matching for employees hired before Dec 31 2020 is immediately vested
Company matching for employees hired after Dec 31 2020 requires 3 years
Basic company contributions require 3 years
Early vesting if you reach age 65, die, or get long-term disability
tests.expected_answer_summary: Vesting depends on contribution type and hire date. Your contributions are always 100% vested. Company match is immediate for pre-2021 hires, 3-year cliff for post-2020 hires. Basic company contributions require 3 years. Exceptions for age 65, death, or disability.

tests.question: Does intern time count toward vesting?
key_facts: Interns are employees if on BNY Mellon payroll
Student interns and co-op employees are eligible to participate
Vesting clock starts on first day as intern
Prior intern service counts toward 3-year vesting requirement
5+ year gap may cause prior service not to count
tests.expected_answer_summary: Yes, intern time counts toward vesting if you were classified as an employee on BNY Mellon's payroll. Your vesting clock starts on your first day as an intern. However, a break in service of 5+ consecutive years may cause prior service not to count.

tests.question: What investment options are available in the plan?
key_facts: 28 investment options total
Tier 1: LifePath target-date funds (2030-2070 plus Retirement)
Tier 2: Passively managed index funds
Tier 3: Actively managed funds
Tier 4: Self-Directed Account for 8000+ mutual funds/ETFs
tests.expected_answer_summary: The plan offers 28 investment options across 4 tiers: Tier 1 has LifePath target-date funds, Tier 2 has low-cost index funds, Tier 3 has actively managed funds across bonds/equity/international, and Tier 4 is a self-directed account for thousands of additional options.

tests.question: Which fund has the lowest expense ratio?
key_facts: BNY Common Stock has 0.0% fee (company stock)
Government Money Market has 0.002% fee (lowest regular fund)
Index funds have low expense ratios at 0.01%
Large Cap Stock Index, Aggregate Bond Index, SMID Cap Stock Index are low cost
tests.expected_answer_summary: BNY Common Stock has 0.0% (company stock). For regular investment funds, Government Money Market is lowest at 0.002%. Index funds tie at 0.01%: Large Cap Stock Index, Aggregate Bond Index, SMID Cap Stock Index.

tests.question: What is the Self-Directed Account and what are its restrictions?
key_facts: Requires $10,000 minimum account balance to open
Minimum initial transfer of $5,000
Maximum 50% of eligible account balance
No individual stocks allowed
Only mutual funds and ETFs
No leveraged or inverse ETFs
No loans or withdrawals from SDA
tests.expected_answer_summary: The SDA lets you invest in additional mutual funds and ETFs beyond core options. Requirements: $10k minimum balance, $5k initial transfer, max 50% of balance. Restrictions: no individual stocks, no leveraged/inverse ETFs, no loans or withdrawals from SDA.

tests.question: What is the minimum transfer amount to the Self-Directed Account?
key_facts: Initial transfer: $5,000
Subsequent transfers: $1,000
Must be whole dollars
Need $10,000 in account to be eligible
tests.expected_answer_summary: Initial transfer minimum is $5,000. Subsequent transfers are $1,000 minimum in whole dollars. You need at least $10,000 in your 401(k) to open an SDA.

tests.question: What are the 2024 contribution limits and does the plan support mega backdoor Roth?
key_facts: Pre-tax plus Roth limit is $23,000
Age 50+ catch-up is $7,500
After-tax contributions up to $25,000
Total annual addition limit $69,000
Mega backdoor Roth is supported
After-tax contributions allowed
In-plan Roth conversions available
Employer match is 100% up to 7% of base pay
Match cap is $16,000 per year
tests.expected_answer_summary: 2024 limits: $23,000 pre-tax/Roth, $7,500 catch-up if 50+, $25,000 after-tax, $69,000 total. Yes, mega backdoor Roth is supported via after-tax contributions plus in-plan Roth conversions. Employer matches 100% up to 7% of pay, capped at $16,000/year.

tests.question: I'm 22 with low risk tolerance, what fund should I pick?
tests.source_reference: General financial guidance based on plan options
key_facts: Default would be LifePath 2065 or 2070 based on age
Low-risk options include Stable Value
Government Money Market is very low risk
Aggregate Bond Index is low-moderate risk
Long time horizon suggests growth is important
Consider blended approach
tests.expected_answer_summary: The default for your age is LifePath 2065/2070 (mostly stocks). For low risk: Stable Value or Government Money Market. However, at 22 you have 40+ years, so consider a blend - mostly LifePath for growth with some Stable Value for comfort.
